chapters.title: Matrices and Determinants

content.overview:
A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers. Matrices are used to organise data and solve systems of linear equations. A
determinant is a scalar associated with a square matrix.
study_notes: For A = [a■■], the order is number of rows × number of columns.
Two matrices can be added only when they have the same order.
For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], det(A) = ad − bc.
A square matrix is invertible when its determinant is non-zero; A■¹ = adj(A)/det(A).
For compatible matrices, generally AB ≠ BA.
content.short_questions:
What is a square matrix?

   Answer: A matrix with the same number of rows and columns.
When does a 2 × 2 matrix have an inverse?

   Answer: When its determinant is non-zero.
content.long_questions:
Find the determinant and inverse of A = [[2,1],[5,3]].

   Solution: det(A) = 2×3 − 1×5 = 1. The adjugate is [[3,−1],[−5,2]]. Therefore A■¹ = [[3,−1],[−5,2]].

mcqs.content: What is the condition for two matrices A of order (m x n) and B of order (p x q) to be multiplied (A * B)? A. m = p B. n = p (columns of A equal rows of B) C. n = q D. m = q Answer: B
What is the order of the product matrix C = A * B if A is (3 x 2) and B is (2 x 4)? A. 3 x 2 B. 3 x 4 C. 2 x 2 D. 4 x 3 Answer: B
A square matrix A is called symmetric if: A. A^T = -A B. A^T = A C. A^2 = I D. det(A) = 0 Answer: B
A square matrix A is called skew-symmetric if: A. A^T = A B. A^T = -A (and all diagonal elements are 0) C. det(A) = 1 D. A * A^T = I Answer: B
A square matrix A is singular if and only if: A. det(A) != 0 B. det(A) = 0 C. Trace(A) = 0 D. A = I Answer: B
What is the formula for the inverse of an invertible square matrix A? A. A^-1 = A^T B. A^-1 = (1 / det(A)) * adj(A) C. A^-1 = det(A) * adj(A) D. A^-1 = -A Answer: B
For any n x n square matrix A, what is A * adj(A)? A. det(A) * A B. det(A) * I C. I D. 0 Answer: B
If A is an n x n matrix and k is a scalar, what is det(k * A)? A. k * det(A) B. k^n * det(A) C. k^2 * det(A) D. n * k * det(A) Answer: B
What is det(A^T) for any square matrix A? A. - det(A) B. det(A) C. 1 / det(A) D. 0 Answer: B
If two rows or two columns of a determinant are identical or proportional, what is the value of the determinant? A. 1 B. 0 C. -1 D. Depends on elements Answer: B
If all elements of a row or column of a determinant are zero, the determinant value is: A. 1 B. 0 C. -1 D. Undefined Answer: B
What is the value of det(A * B) for two square matrices of the same order? A. det(A) + det(B) B. det(A) * det(B) C. det(A) / det(B) D. 0 Answer: B
What is (A * B)^T equal to by the reversal law of transpose? A. A^T * B^T B. B^T * A^T C. A * B D. - B^T * A^T Answer: B
What is (A * B)^-1 equal to for invertible matrices A and B? A. A^-1 * B^-1 B. B^-1 * A^-1 C. A * B D. B^-1 + A^-1 Answer: B
What is the trace of a square matrix? A. Determinant of matrix B. Sum of the main diagonal elements C. Product of diagonal elements D. Number of rows Answer: B

In Cramer's rule for a system of 3 linear equations, when does a unique solution exist? A. det(D) = 0 B. det(D) != 0 (where D is the coefficient determinant) C. D1 = D2 = D3 = 0 D. D = infinity Answer: B

In Cramer's rule, if D = 0 and at least one of Dx, Dy, Dz is non-zero, the system of equations has: A. Unique solution B. No solution (inconsistent system) C. Infinitely many solutions D. Trivial solution Answer: B
What is an idempotent matrix A? A. A^2 = 0 B. A^2 = A C. A^2 = I D. A^T = A Answer: B
What is an orthogonal matrix A? A. A^T = -A B. A * A^T = A^T * A = I (or A^-1 = A^T) C. A^2 = I D. det(A) = 0 Answer: B
What is the determinant of a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]]? A. a*c - b*d B. a*d - b*c C. a*b - c*d D. a*d + b*c Answer: B

1ST PAPER — Chapter 1: Matrices and Determinants
Chapter overview
A matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers. Matrices are used to organise data and solve systems of linear equations. A
determinant is a scalar associated with a square matrix.

Key concepts and important formulas
• For A = [a■■], the order is number of rows × number of columns.

• Two matrices can be added only when they have the same order.

• For a 2 × 2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]], det(A) = ad − bc.

• A square matrix is invertible when its determinant is non-zero; A■¹ = adj(A)/det(A).

• For compatible matrices, generally AB ≠ BA.

Short-answer practice — answers
What is a square matrix?

   Answer: A matrix with the same number of rows and columns.
When does a 2 × 2 matrix have an inverse?

   Answer: When its determinant is non-zero.

Long-answer practice — worked solution
Find the determinant and inverse of A = [[2,1],[5,3]].

   Solution: det(A) = 2×3 − 1×5 = 1. The adjugate is [[3,−1],[−5,2]]. Therefore A■¹ = [[3,−1],[−5,2]].

Multiple-choice questions
1. The determinant of [[a,b],[c,d]] is:

A. ad − bc     B. ab − cd   C. ac − bd   D. ad + bc

Answer: A

2. A square matrix is singular if its determinant is:

A. 1   B. −1    C. 0   D. Non-zero

Answer: C

chapters.title: Vectors

content.overview:
A vector has magnitude and direction. Vectors describe displacement, velocity and force. Vector operations allow geometric and
physical quantities to be resolved and combined.
study_notes: In two dimensions, a = a■i + a■j.
Magnitude: |a| = √(a■² + a■²).
Dot product: a·b = |a||b|cosθ; it is a scalar.
Cross-product magnitude: |a×b| = |a||b|sinθ.
The resultant of vectors is found by adding corresponding components.
content.short_questions:
Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper                                                                                      Page 3

What is a unit vector?

   Answer: A vector of magnitude one that specifies direction.
When is the dot product zero?

   Answer: When the two non-zero vectors are perpendicular.
content.long_questions:
Find the magnitude and direction of v = 3i + 4j.

   Solution: |v| = √(3²+4²) = 5. Its angle from the positive x-axis is θ = tan■¹(4/3) ≈ 53.13°.

mcqs.content: What is the unit vector in the direction of vector A? A. A * |A| B. A / |A| C. |A| / A D. A x A Answer: B
If A = a1 i + a2 j + a3 k, what is the magnitude |A|? A. a1 + a2 + a3 B. sqrt(a1^2 + a2^2 + a3^2) C. a1^2 + a2^2 + a3^2 D. sqrt(a1*a2*a3) Answer: B
What are the direction cosines l, m, n of a vector satisfying? A. l + m + n = 1 B. l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1 C. l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 0 D. l*m*n = 1 Answer: B
What is the dot product of vectors A = 2i + 3j - k and B = i - 2j + 4k? A. 2 - 6 - 4 = -8 B. 2 + 6 + 4 = 12 C. -8 D. 0 Answer: A
What is the angle theta between two vectors A and B? A. cos theta = (A . B) / (|A| * |B|) B. sin theta = (A . B) / (|A| * |B|) C. cos theta = |A x B| / (|A| * |B|) D. tan theta = A . B Answer: A
What is the projection of vector A on vector B? A. (A . B) / |A| B. (A . B) / |B| C. (A x B) / |B| D. |A| * |B| Answer: B
What is the vector component of A along B? A. ((A . B) / |B|) * (B / |B|) = ((A . B) / |B|^2) * B B. (A . B) * B C. (A x B) / |B| D. B / |B| Answer: A
Two vectors A and B are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if: A. A x B = 0 B. A . B = 0 C. |A| = |B| D. A + B = 0 Answer: B
Two non-zero vectors A and B are collinear (parallel) if and only if: A. A . B = 0 B. A x B = 0 (or A = k * B) C. A + B = 0 D. |A| = |B| Answer: B

What is the scalar triple product of three vectors A, B, C representing? A. Area of triangle B. Volume of the parallelepiped formed by A, B, C (V = [A B C] = A . (B x C)) C. Surface area D. Work done Answer: B
Three vectors A, B, C are coplanar if and only if their scalar triple product is: A. 1 B. 0 ([A B C] = 0) C. -1 D. Infinite Answer: B
In vector triple product, what is A x (B x C)? A. (A . B) C - (A . C) B B. (A . C) B - (A . B) C (BAC-CAB rule) C. (B . C) A - (A . B) C D. 0 Answer: B
What is i . (j x k)? A. 0 B. 1 (i . i = 1) C. -1 D. k Answer: B
What is the position vector of the midpoint of the line segment joining points with position vectors A and B? A. A - B B. (A + B) / 2 C. (A + B) / 3 D. 2 * (A + B) Answer: B

What is the position vector of the point dividing the join of A and B internally in ratio m:n? A. (m*A + n*B) / (m + n) B. (m*B + n*A) / (m + n) C. (m*B - n*A) / (m - n) D. (A + B) / (m + n) Answer: B
What is the position vector of the centroid G of a triangle with vertices position vectors A, B, C? A. (A + B + C) / 2 B. (A + B + C) / 3 C. A + B + C D. (A + B + C) / 4 Answer: B
Work done by a force F causing a displacement d is given by the vector formula: A. W = F x d B. W = F . d C. W = |F| / |d| D. W = (1/2) F . d Answer: B
What is the moment of a force F about a point with position vector r? A. r . F B. r x F (Torque) C. F x r D. r * F Answer: B
If |A + B| = |A - B|, what is the angle between vectors A and B? A. 0° B. 90° (vectors are perpendicular) C. 180° D. 45° Answer: B
If A + B + C = 0 and |A| = 3, |B| = 5, |C| = 7, what is the angle between A and B? A. 30° B. 60° (cos theta = (49 - 9 - 25) / 30 = 15/30 = 1/2) C. 45° D. 90° Answer: B

chapters.title: Straight Lines

content.overview:
Coordinate geometry represents geometric objects using equations. A straight line may be described by its slope and a point, two
points, intercepts or a general linear equation.
study_notes: Slope m = (y■−y■)/(x■−x■), where x■ ≠ x■.
Point-slope form: y−y■ = m(x−x■).
Slope-intercept form: y = mx+c.
Parallel non-vertical lines have equal slopes; perpendicular lines satisfy m■m■ = −1.
The general form is ax+by+c=0.
content.short_questions:
What is the slope of a horizontal line?

   Answer: Zero.
State the condition for two non-vertical lines to be perpendicular.

   Answer: Their slopes have product −1.
content.long_questions:
Find the equation of the line through (2,3) and (4,7).

   Solution: Slope m = (7−3)/(4−2) = 2. Using y−3 = 2(x−2), the equation is y = 2x−1.

mcqs.content: What is the distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) in Cartesian plane? A. sqrt((x2 - x1) + (y2 - y1)) B. sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2) C. (x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 D. abs(x2 - x1) + abs(y2 - y1) Answer: B

What are the coordinates of the point dividing the line segment joining (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) internally in ratio m:n? A. ((m*x2 + n*x1)/(m+n), (m*y2 + n*y1)/(m+n)) B. ((m*x1 + n*x2)/(m+n), (m*y1 + n*y2)/(m+n)) C. ((m*x2 - n*x1)/(m-n), (m*y2 - n*y1)/(m-n)) D. ((x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2) Answer: A

What is the area of a triangle with vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3)? A. (1/2) * |x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)| B. x1*y2 + x2*y3 + x3*y1 C. (1/2) * (x1 + x2 + x3) D. abs(x1*y1 + x2*y2 + x3*y3) Answer: A
What is the slope (gradient) m of a straight line making an angle theta with positive x-axis? A. sin theta B. tan theta (or (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1)) C. cos theta D. cot theta Answer: B
What is the slope-intercept form of the equation of a straight line? A. x/a + y/b = 1 B. y = m*x + c C. A*x + B*y + C = 0 D. y - y1 = m*(x - x1) Answer: B
What is the intercept form of a straight line making intercepts a and b on x and y axes? A. x/b + y/a = 1 B. x/a + y/b = 1 C. a*x + b*y = 1 D. x*a + y*b = 0 Answer: B

What is the normal (perpendicular) form of a straight line (normal length p, angle alpha with x-axis)? A. x * sin alpha + y * cos alpha = p B. x * cos alpha + y * sin alpha = p C. x * tan alpha + y = p D. x/cos alpha + y/sin alpha = p Answer: B
What is the slope of the line A*x + B*y + C = 0? A. A / B B. - A / B C. - B / A D. C / B Answer: B
What is the condition for two lines with slopes m1 and m2 to be parallel? A. m1 * m2 = -1 B. m1 = m2 C. m1 + m2 = 0 D. m1 * m2 = 1 Answer: B
What is the condition for two straight lines with slopes m1 and m2 to be perpendicular? A. m1 = m2 B. m1 * m2 = -1 C. m1 + m2 = 0 D. m1 * m2 = 1 Answer: B

What is the angle theta between two lines with slopes m1 and m2? A. tan theta = +/-( (m1 - m2) / (1 + m1 * m2) ) B. tan theta = (m1 + m2) / (1 - m1*m2) C. cos theta = m1 * m2 D. sin theta = m1 - m2 Answer: A

What is the perpendicular distance d from point (x1, y1) to the line A*x + B*y + C = 0? A. abs(A*x1 + B*y1 + C) / (A^2 + B^2) B. abs(A*x1 + B*y1 + C) / sqrt(A^2 + B^2) C. abs(A*x1 + B*y1) / sqrt(A^2 + B^2) D. A*x1 + B*y1 + C Answer: B

What is the distance d between two parallel lines A*x + B*y + C1 = 0 and A*x + B*y + C2 = 0? A. abs(C1 + C2) / sqrt(A^2 + B^2) B. abs(C1 - C2) / sqrt(A^2 + B^2) C. abs(C1 - C2) / (A^2 + B^2) D. abs(C1 - C2) Answer: B
The equation of a line parallel to A*x + B*y + C = 0 is: A. B*x - A*y + k = 0 B. A*x + B*y + k = 0 C. A*x - B*y + k = 0 D. x + y + k = 0 Answer: B
The equation of a line perpendicular to A*x + B*y + C = 0 is: A. A*x + B*y + k = 0 B. B*x - A*y + k = 0 C. B*x + A*y + k = 0 D. A*x - B*y + k = 0 Answer: B

What are the coordinates of the centroid of a triangle with vertices (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (x3, y3)? A. ((x1+x2+x3)/2, (y1+y2+y3)/2) B. ((x1+x2+x3)/3, (y1+y2+y3)/3) C. (x1+x2+x3, y1+y2+y3) D. ((x1*x2*x3)/3, (y1*y2*y3)/3) Answer: B
What is the point of intersection of the three medians of a triangle? A. Orthocenter B. Centroid C. Incenter D. Circumcenter Answer: B
What is the point of intersection of the three altitudes of a triangle? A. Centroid B. Orthocenter C. Circumcenter D. Incenter Answer: B
What is the point of intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the sides of a triangle? A. Orthocenter B. Circumcenter C. Incenter D. Centroid Answer: B
In what ratio does the centroid G divide each median from vertex to base? A. 1 : 1 B. 2 : 1 C. 3 : 1 D. 1 : 2 Answer: B

chapters.title: Circles

content.overview: A circle is the locus of points at a fixed distance from a fixed centre. Its equation follows from the distance formula.
study_notes: Standard form: (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r².
Centre-radius form x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 has centre (−g,−f).
Radius = √(g²+f²−c).
A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.
A point lies inside, on or outside a circle according as its centre distance is less than, equal to or greater than r.
content.short_questions:
What is the radius of x²+y²=r²?

   Answer: The radius is r and the centre is (0,0).
What is the relation between a tangent and the radius at contact?

   Answer: They are perpendicular.
content.long_questions:
Find the centre and radius of x²+y²−4x+6y−12=0.

   Solution: Complete squares: (x−2)²−4+(y+3)²−9−12=0. Thus (x−2)²+(y+3)²=25. Centre = (2,−3), radius = 5.

mcqs.content: What is the standard equation of a circle with center (h, k) and radius r? A. (x + h)^2 + (y + k)^2 = r^2 B. (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 C. x^2 + y^2 = r^2 D. (x - h)^2 - (y - k)^2 = r^2 Answer: B

What are the center and radius of the general circle x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0? A. Center (g, f), radius sqrt(g^2 + f^2) B. Center (-g, -f), radius sqrt(g^2 + f^2 - c) C. Center (-g, -f), radius g^2 + f^2 - c D. Center (g, f), radius sqrt(g^2 + f^2 + c) Answer: B

What is the condition for the general equation of second degree to represent a circle? A. h = 0 and a = b (coefficient of x^2 equals coefficient of y^2 and no xy term) B. h != 0 and a = b C. a = -b D. c = 0 Answer: A
What is the condition for a circle x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 to touch the x-axis? A. f^2 = c B. g^2 = c C. g^2 + f^2 = c D. g = 0 Answer: B
What is the condition for a circle to touch the y-axis? A. g^2 = c B. f^2 = c C. f = 0 D. c = 0 Answer: B
What is the length of intercept cut off by the circle on the x-axis? A. 2 * sqrt(f^2 - c) B. 2 * sqrt(g^2 - c) C. sqrt(g^2 - c) D. 2 * g Answer: B
What is the length of intercept cut off by the circle on the y-axis? A. 2 * sqrt(g^2 - c) B. 2 * sqrt(f^2 - c) C. sqrt(f^2 - c) D. 2 * f Answer: B

What is the condition for the line y = mx + c to be a tangent to the circle x^2 + y^2 = a^2? A. c = a * m B. c^2 = a^2 * (1 + m^2) (or c = +/- a * sqrt(1 + m^2)) C. c = a / m D. c^2 = a^2 * (1 - m^2) Answer: B
What is the equation of the tangent to the circle x^2 + y^2 = a^2 at point (x1, y1)? A. x1*y + y1*x = a^2 B. x*x1 + y*y1 = a^2 C. x*x1 - y*y1 = a^2 D. x/x1 + y/y1 = 1 Answer: B

What is the equation of the normal to the circle x^2 + y^2 = a^2 at point (x1, y1)? A. x*y1 - y*x1 = 0 (or y = (y1/x1)*x, passes through center) B. x*x1 + y*y1 = a^2 C. x*y1 + y*x1 = 0 D. x - y = x1 - y1 Answer: A

What is the length of the tangent from external point (x1, y1) to circle x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0? A. x1^2 + y1^2 + 2gx1 + 2fy1 + c B. sqrt(x1^2 + y1^2 + 2gx1 + 2fy1 + c) = sqrt(S1) C. 2 * sqrt(S1) D. S1 / 2 Answer: B
What is the condition for two circles with centers C1, C2 and radii r1, r2 to touch externally? A. C1C2 = r1 - r2 B. C1C2 = r1 + r2 C. C1C2 < r1 + r2 D. C1C2 = 0 Answer: B
What is the condition for two circles to touch internally? A. C1C2 = r1 + r2 B. C1C2 = abs(r1 - r2) C. C1C2 = 0 D. C1C2 > r1 + r2 Answer: B

What is the condition for two circles to intersect orthogonally (at right angles)? A. 2(g1*g2 + f1*f2) = c1 + c2 B. g1*g2 + f1*f2 = c1*c2 C. 2(g1*f2 + g2*f1) = c1 + c2 D. g1 = g2 and f1 = f2 Answer: A
What is the equation of the radical axis of two circles S1 = 0 and S2 = 0? A. S1 + S2 = 0 B. S1 - S2 = 0 (straight line) C. S1 * S2 = 0 D. S1 / S2 = 1 Answer: B

What is the equation of the circle having (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) as endpoints of a diameter? A. (x - x1)(y - y1) + (x - x2)(y - y2) = 0 B. (x - x1)(x - x2) + (y - y1)(y - y2) = 0 C. (x - x1)^2 + (y - y2)^2 = 0 D. (x1 - x2)^2 + (y1 - y2)^2 = r^2 Answer: B
How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from an external point? A. 1 B. 2 (of equal lengths) C. Infinitely many D. 0 Answer: B
How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from an internal point? A. 1 B. 0 (no tangent possible) C. 2 D. Infinitely many Answer: B

What is the power of a point P(x1, y1) with respect to circle S = 0? A. Length of chord B. S1 = x1^2 + y1^2 + 2gx1 + 2fy1 + c (positive outside, zero on circle, negative inside) C. Radius squared D. Distance to center Answer: B
If point (x1, y1) lies on the circle x^2 + y^2 = a^2, what is x1^2 + y1^2 - a^2? A. Greater than 0 B. Equal to 0 C. Less than 0 D. Equal to a Answer: B

A circle is the locus of points at a fixed distance from a fixed centre. Its equation follows from the distance formula.

Key concepts and important formulas
• Standard form: (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r².

• Centre-radius form x²+y²+2gx+2fy+c=0 has centre (−g,−f).

• Radius = √(g²+f²−c).

• A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

• A point lies inside, on or outside a circle according as its centre distance is less than, equal to or greater than r.

Short-answer practice — answers
What is the radius of x²+y²=r²?

   Answer: The radius is r and the centre is (0,0).
What is the relation between a tangent and the radius at contact?

   Answer: They are perpendicular.

Long-answer practice — worked solution
Find the centre and radius of x²+y²−4x+6y−12=0.

   Solution: Complete squares: (x−2)²−4+(y+3)²−9−12=0. Thus (x−2)²+(y+3)²=25. Centre = (2,−3), radius = 5.

A. 5   B. 7   C. 14   D. 49

Answer: B

A. Diameter anywhere     B. Radius at contact   C. Chord always   D. Secant

Answer: B

real number system.

content.short_questions:
What is an irrational number?

   Answer: A real number that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers.

mcqs.content: Which of the following is an irrational number? A. 3/4 B. sqrt(2) (non-terminating, non-repeating) C. 0.333... D. sqrt(9) Answer: B

What is the supremum (least upper bound) of the open interval (2, 5)? A. 2 B. 5 C. 5.1 D. Does not exist Answer: B

According to Archimedean property of real numbers, for any real x, there exists a natural number n such that: A. n < x B. n > x C. n = x D. n * x = 1 Answer: B

content.overview:
Linear programming optimises a linear objective function subject to linear constraints. The feasible region is formed by the
constraints.
study_notes: Write the objective function in terms of decision variables.
Convert resource limits into linear inequalities.
Graph each boundary line and identify the feasible region.

content.short_questions:
Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper                                                                                      Page 10

What is a feasible region?

   Answer: The set of points satisfying all constraints simultaneously.
Where is the optimum of a linear objective function found for a bounded polygonal feasible region?

   Answer: At at least one vertex (corner point) of the feasible region.
content.long_questions:
Maximise P=3x+2y subject to x≥0, y≥0, x+y≤4, x≤2.

   Solution: The feasible vertices are (0,0), (2,0), (2,2), (0,4). P values are 0, 6, 10, 8 respectively. Maximum P=10 at (2,2).

mcqs.content: In a linear programming problem (LPP), what is the function to be maximized or minimized called? A. Constraint function B. Objective function (Z = ax + by) C. Feasible function D. Slack variable Answer: B
What type of mathematical relationships must both the objective function and constraints satisfy in LPP? A. Quadratic B. Linear (degree 1 in all variables) C. Exponential D. Non-linear Answer: B
The non-negativity restrictions in standard LPP are represented by: A. x <= 0, y <= 0 B. x >= 0, y >= 0 (first quadrant) C. x + y >= 0 D. x * y >= 0 Answer: B
What is the collection of all points satisfying all the linear constraints of an LPP called? A. Infeasible region B. Feasible region (solution space) C. Unbounded plane D. Optimum region Answer: B
What geometric property does the feasible region of any linear programming problem always possess? A. Concave set B. Convex polygon / convex set C. Circular disc D. Non-convex set Answer: B

According to the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Programming, where does the optimal (maximum or minimum) value of the objective function occur? A. At the origin only B. At one or more corner points (vertices / extreme points) of the feasible region C. In the interior of feasible region D. At infinity only Answer: B

If the feasible region of an LPP is bounded, what can be said about the maximum and minimum values of Z? A. Neither exists B. Both maximum and minimum values of Z exist C. Only maximum exists D. Only minimum exists Answer: B

If two corner points of a feasible region yield the same optimal value of Z, then: A. No solution exists B. Every point on the line segment joining these two vertices is also an optimal solution (infinitely many solutions) C. The problem is inconsistent D. Only the midpoint is optimal Answer: B
What is an unbounded feasible region in LPP? A. A region that has no corner points B. A feasible region that extends indefinitely in at least one direction C. A single point D. Empty set Answer: B

What happens when the constraints of an LPP have no common point satisfying all of them? A. Multiple optimal solutions B. No feasible solution (infeasible problem) C. Degenerate solution D. Unbounded solution Answer: B
In the graphical method of LPP, the lines representing the constraints are called: A. Isocost lines B. Boundary lines C. Objective lines D. Axes Answer: B

What is an iso-profit or iso-cost line in LPP graphical solution? A. A constraint boundary B. A line along which the objective function Z has a constant value (Z = c) C. Coordinate axis D. 45° line Answer: B
A non-negative variable added to a '<=' constraint to convert it into an equality is called a: A. Surplus variable B. Slack variable C. Artificial variable D. Basic variable Answer: B
A non-negative variable subtracted from a '>=' constraint to convert it into an equality is called a: A. Slack variable B. Surplus variable C. Unrestricted variable D. Scalar Answer: B

What algorithm developed by George Dantzig in 1947 solves general multi-variable LPPs algebraically? A. Newton-Raphson method B. Simplex method / Simplex algorithm C. Euler method D. Gauss-Seidel method Answer: B

For the objective function Z = 3x + 4y with corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (2, 3), and (0, 5), what is the maximum value of Z? A. 12 B. 20 (at corner point (0, 5): 3*0 + 4*5 = 20) C. 18 D. 16 Answer: B

What is the dual of a linear programming problem? A. Inverse function B. An associated LPP derived systematically from the primal problem whose optimal value equals that of primal C. Negative of primal D. Complement of set Answer: B

Can the optimal solution of a linear programming problem occur strictly in the interior of the feasible region? A. Always B. No, it always occurs on the boundary, specifically at extreme vertices C. Only for maximization D. Only if variables are negative Answer: B

What is a redundant constraint in an LPP? A. A constraint that cannot be satisfied B. A constraint whose removal does not alter the feasible region C. The non-negativity constraint D. The objective function Answer: B

   Solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by (1+i): [(3+2i)(1+i)]/2 = (1+5i)/2 = 1/2 + (5/2)i.

content.overview:
Conic sections are curves formed by intersecting a plane with a double cone. The main conics are the circle, parabola, ellipse and
hyperbola.
study_notes: A parabola is the locus of points equidistant from a focus and directrix.
For y²=4ax, focus=(a,0), directrix x=−a.

What is the moment of a force?

Bangladesh HSC Higher Mathematics | First & Second Paper                                                                                      Page 14

Two perpendicular forces of 6 N and 8 N act at a point. Find their resultant magnitude.

Forces must be represented in magnitude and direction by the sides of a closed triangle taken in order C. Forces must be collinear D. Forces must be perpendicular Answer: B

What is a couple in mechanics? A. Two equal and like parallel forces B. Two equal, opposite, non-collinear parallel forces C. Two perpendicular forces D. Single force Answer: B
What is the moment of a couple (torque)? A. Force + arm B. Magnitude of either force * perpendicular distance between their lines of action (arm of couple) C. Force / arm D. Zero Answer: B

Can a couple be equilibrated by a single force? A. Yes, if force is large B. No, a couple can only be balanced by another couple of equal and opposite moment C. Always D. Depends on friction Answer: B

According to Varignon's Theorem of moments, the algebraic sum of moments of two coplanar forces about any point equals: A. Zero B. The moment of their resultant about that same point C. Product of moments D. Sum of forces Answer: B

What are the conditions of equilibrium for a system of coplanar forces? A. sum Fx = 0, sum Fy = 0, and sum M = 0 (sum of moments about any point is zero) B. sum Fx = 0 only C. sum M = 0 only D. sum Fx = sum Fy Answer: A

If three forces acting on a rigid body keep it in equilibrium, their lines of action must be: A. Skew lines B. Either all parallel or all concurrent at a single point C. Mutually perpendicular D. Closed loop Answer: B

What is the angle of friction lambda defined as (where mu is coefficient of static friction)? A. sin lambda = mu B. tan lambda = mu (or lambda = tan^-1(mu)) C. cos lambda = mu D. lambda = mu Answer: B

What is the angle of repose theta_r of an inclined plane? A. Angle where body accelerates B. Maximum inclination of plane with horizontal at which a body placed on it remains at rest without slipping (theta_r = lambda) C. 90° D. 45° always Answer: B
What is the center of gravity (CG) of a uniform solid triangular lamina (plate)? A. Orthocenter B. Centroid (intersection of medians, at height h/3 from base) C. Circumcenter D. Incenter Answer: B

content.overview:
This chapter applies vectors and kinematics to particle motion in two dimensions, including projectile motion and motion under
gravity.
study_notes: Velocity is the time rate of change of position; acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
For constant acceleration, v=u+at and s=ut+½at² in one dimension.
Projectile horizontal velocity is constant when air resistance is neglected.
For launch and landing at the same level: T=2u sinθ/g; H=u²sin²θ/(2g); R=u²sin2θ/g.
At the highest point of projectile motion, vertical velocity is zero.
content.short_questions:
What is projectile motion?

   Answer: Two-dimensional motion of an object projected into the air and then moving under gravity, neglecting air resistance.
What is the vertical velocity at the highest point?

   Answer: Zero.
content.long_questions:
A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. Find its time of flight, taking g=10 m/s².

   Solution: T=2u sinθ/g = 2×20×0.5/10 = 2 s.

mcqs.content: A particle moves in a straight line with uniform acceleration f. What is displacement s after time t? A. s = ut + ft B. s = ut + (1/2) * f * t^2 C. s = (1/2) f t^2 D. s = u t^2 Answer: B

What is the distance traveled in the nth second by a particle with initial velocity u and acceleration f? A. s_n = u + f * n B. s_n = u + (1/2) * f * (2n - 1) C. s_n = u + (1/2) f n^2 D. s_n = (2n - 1) f Answer: B
A body is projected vertically upwards with speed u. What is the maximum height H reached (g = acceleration due to gravity)? A. u / 2g B. H = u^2 / (2g) C. 2u^2 / g D. u^2 / g Answer: B
What is the total time of flight T for a body projected vertically upward with speed u? A. u / g B. T = 2u / g C. u^2 / 2g D. sqrt(2u / g) Answer: B

A body projected vertically upwards takes time t1 to reach height h on its way up and t2 on its way down. What is h? A. (1/2) g (t1 + t2) B. (1/2) * g * t1 * t2 C. g * t1 * t2 D. sqrt(t1 * t2) Answer: B
What is the total time of flight (t1 + t2) for the body projected vertically upward? A. 2u / g B. t1 + t2 = 2u / g C. u / g D. sqrt(2h / g) Answer: B

What is the equation of the trajectory of a projectile launched with speed u at angle alpha? A. y = x * sin alpha - (g*x^2)/(2u^2) B. y = x * tan alpha - (g * x^2) / (2 * u^2 * cos^2 alpha) C. y = x * tan alpha + g*x^2 D. y = x^2 / (2u^2) Answer: B
What is the horizontal range R of a projectile launched at angle alpha with speed u? A. u^2 * sin alpha / g B. R = (u^2 * sin(2*alpha)) / g C. u^2 * cos(2*alpha) / g D. 2u^2 * sin alpha / g Answer: B
What is the maximum horizontal range R_max achievable with speed u? A. u^2 / 2g B. R_max = u^2 / g (at launch angle alpha = 45°) C. 2u^2 / g D. u / g Answer: B

What is the relation between maximum height H and maximum horizontal range R_max (at 45°)? A. H = R_max B. H = R_max / 4 (since H = u^2/4g and R_max = u^2/g) C. H = R_max / 2 D. H = 2 * R_max Answer: B
What is the velocity v of a projectile at its highest point? A. Zero B. v = u * cos alpha (only horizontal component remains) C. u * sin alpha D. u Answer: B
At what angle of projection is the horizontal range R equal to the maximum height H? A. 45° B. alpha = tan^-1(4) (~76°) C. 60° D. 30° Answer: B

What is the time of flight T of a projectile launched on an inclined plane of slope beta with angle alpha to horizontal? A. 2u sin(alpha - beta) / (g cos beta) B. 2u sin alpha / g C. 2u cos alpha / g D. u^2 / g Answer: A
In relative motion, what is the velocity of body A relative to body B (v_AB)? A. v_A + v_B B. v_A - v_B C. v_B - v_A D. v_A * v_B Answer: B

A rain drop falls vertically at 4 m/s and a person walks horizontally at 3 m/s. What is the apparent speed of rain felt by person? A. 1 m/s B. 5 m/s (sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = 5 m/s) C. 7 m/s D. 12 m/s Answer: B
At what angle with the vertical must the person hold their umbrella to protect from rain? A. tan^-1(4/3) B. tan^-1(3/4) (~37° inclined forward) C. 45° D. 90° Answer: B
What is the tangential acceleration a_t in non-uniform circular motion (speed v, radius r)? A. v^2 / r B. a_t = dv / dt C. omega^2 * r D. 0 Answer: B
What is the total acceleration a in non-uniform circular motion? A. a_t + a_c B. a = sqrt(a_t^2 + a_c^2) (where a_c = v^2/r) C. a_t * a_c D. a_c - a_t Answer: B

Two particles are projected simultaneously from the same point with equal speeds at complementary angles alpha and (90° - alpha). Their times of flight t1 and t2 satisfy: A. t1 = t2 B. t1 / t2 = tan alpha C. t1 * t2 = 2R / g D. Both B and C are correct Answer: D
A stone dropped from a balloon rising vertically with speed u at height h hits the ground with initial velocity: A. 0 B. u upwards (kinematics: -h = ut - (1/2)gt^2) C. u downwards D. 2u Answer: B

chapters.title: Measures of Dispersion and Probability

content.overview:
Statistics summarises data, while measures of dispersion describe its spread. Probability quantifies uncertainty for random
events.
study_notes: Range = maximum − minimum.
Variance is the mean squared deviation from the arithmetic mean (with convention depending on population/sample).
Standard deviation is the positive square root of variance.
For equally likely outcomes, P(A)=favourable outcomes/total outcomes.
P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B); for independent events P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).
content.short_questions:
What is range?

   Answer: The difference between the largest and smallest observations.
What is the probability of an impossible event?

   Answer: Zero.
content.long_questions:
A fair die is rolled once. Find the probability of obtaining an even number.

   Solution: Even outcomes are {2,4,6}, three of six equally likely outcomes. Probability=3/6=1/2.

mcqs.content: Which measure of central tendency is affected most by extreme values (outliers)? A. Median B. Arithmetic Mean (AM) C. Mode D. Geometric Mean Answer: B
What is the median of an ordered dataset of n observations when n is odd? A. Observation at (n/2) B. Observation at ((n + 1) / 2)th position C. (n + 1) / 2 D. Average of all Answer: B
What is the mode of a dataset? A. The arithmetic average B. The value that occurs with greatest frequency C. The middle value D. Highest value minus lowest Answer: B

What is the empirical relation between Mean, Median, and Mode for moderately skewed distribution? A. Mean - Mode = Median B. Mode = 3 * Median - 2 * Mean C. Median = 3 * Mode - 2 * Mean D. Mode = 2 * Median - Mean Answer: B
What is range in measures of dispersion? A. Variance B. Difference between the maximum and minimum observations (Range = X_max - X_min) C. Standard deviation D. Mean deviation Answer: B

What is the variance sigma^2 formula for n observations x1, x2... xn with mean x_bar? A. sum (xi - x_bar) / n B. sigma^2 = (1 / n) * sum (xi - x_bar)^2 = (1/n) sum xi^2 - (x_bar)^2 C. sqrt(sum xi^2) D. sum xi / n Answer: B
What is standard deviation (sigma)? A. Variance squared B. Positive square root of variance (sigma = sqrt(Variance)) C. Mean deviation D. Range / 2 Answer: B

What is the coefficient of variation (CV) used to compare dispersion of two datasets? A. (Mean / SD) * 100 B. CV = (Standard Deviation / Mean) * 100 = (sigma / x_bar) * 100 C. Variance * 100 D. SD * Mean Answer: B

If all observations in a dataset are increased by a constant c (y = x + c), what happens to variance and standard deviation? A. Increases by c B. Remains completely unchanged (variance is independent of change of origin) C. Multiplied by c D. Becomes zero Answer: B

If all observations are multiplied by a constant c (y = c * x), what is the new standard deviation? A. sigma_x B. |c| * sigma_x (variance is multiplied by c^2) C. c^2 * sigma_x D. sigma_x / c Answer: B
What is the sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean (sum (xi - x_bar))? A. n B. Zero (always 0 by definition of mean) C. 1 D. Variance Answer: B

What is the classical definition of probability P(A) of an event A with m favorable outcomes and n total equally likely outcomes? A. P(A) = n / m B. P(A) = m / n (where 0 <= P(A) <= 1) C. P(A) = m * n D. P(A) = m + n Answer: B
What is the probability of the sure (certain) event S and impossible event phi? A. P(S) = 0, P(phi) = 1 B. P(S) = 1, P(phi) = 0 C. P(S) = 0.5, P(phi) = 0.5 D. P(S) = infinity Answer: B
For any event A, what is P(A) + P(A') (where A' is the complementary event)? A. 0 B. 1 C. 2 D. P(A) Answer: B
What is the addition rule of probability for any two events A and B? A. P(A U B) = P(A) + P(B) B. P(A U B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A cap B) C. P(A U B) = P(A) * P(B) D. P(A U B) = P(A) / P(B) Answer: B
Two events A and B are mutually exclusive (disjoint) if and only if: A. P(A) = P(B) B. P(A cap B) = 0 (they cannot occur simultaneously) C. P(A cap B) = P(A)*P(B) D. A = B Answer: B
Two events A and B are statistically independent if and only if: A. P(A cap B) = 0 B. P(A cap B) = P(A) * P(B) C. P(A U B) = 1 D. P(A) + P(B) = 1 Answer: B
What is the conditional probability P(A | B) of event A given that event B has occurred (P(B) > 0)? A. P(A) / P(B) B. P(A cap B) / P(B) C. P(A U B) / P(B) D. P(A) * P(B) Answer: B

What is the probability of getting an even number or a prime number in a single roll of an unbiased six-sided die? A. 3/6 B. 5/6 (events: {2, 3, 4, 5, 6} out of {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}) C. 4/6 D. 1 Answer: B

In a binomial probability distribution with n trials and success probability p, what are the mean and variance? A. Mean = n*p, Variance = n*p*q (where q = 1 - p) B. Mean = n/p, Variance = n*p C. Mean = p, Variance = p*q D. Mean = n*p, Variance = sqrt(n*p*q) Answer: A
